## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Single-blind (reviewers anonymous to authors; authors' identities known to reviewers). Editor-in-Chief selects and invites reviewers; two complete reviews typically required before an accept decision; major revisions return to original reviewers, minor revisions may be checked by the Editor-in-Chief alone; special issues use Guest Editors who still route final decisions through the EiC. |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — WO2 defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Publisher-wide Springer Nature policy applies (journal-specific submission guidelines page reiterates it, not a bespoke UMUAI policy). LLMs (e.g. ChatGPT) cannot be listed as authors and any substantive LLM use in writing the manuscript must be disclosed in the Methods section (or equivalent). 'AI-assisted copy editing' (grammar/readability polishing of human-written text) is explicitly exempt from disclosure. Generative AI-generated images are not allowed in publications. Peer reviewers are separately asked not to upload manuscripts into generative AI tools (confidentiality rule, not an author-facing gate). Net effect: permission gate is conditional -- silent light copy-editing use is fine, disclosed substantive drafting/analysis use is fine, undisclosed substantive use or AI authorship/AI images are not. |
| **Source URL** | https://link.springer.com/journal/11257/submission-guidelines (via idp.springer.com redirect); https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies |

### Preprint Policy

> WO2 research note (not broken down per-stage — see docs/workorders/WO2_SOFT_METADATA_BATCH.md for why): Not stated explicitly on the journal's own submission-guidelines page. Falls back to Springer Nature's publisher-wide unified policy, which 'encourages posting of preprints on preprint servers, supports citation and open licensing of preprints,' subject to authors respecting Springer Nature's media-communication policies. The journal page only states manuscripts must be original and 'not have been published elsewhere in any form or language' -- standard prior-publication language; Springer's general practice treats preprints as not constituting prior publication, but UMUAI itself does not confirm this in its own guidelines.
> Source: https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies

**Current positioning (WO2, what the journal accepts now):** Reviewing DBLP-listed 2025 (Vol 35) and 2026 (Vol 36, through Sept issue) tables of contents, the journal is currently publishing: recommender systems research (graph-based/hypergraph, sequential, conversational, contrastive/self-supervised, fairness/de-biasing, autoregressive generation, cross-domain nudging), adaptive/intelligent tutoring and learning-analytics work (rule learning, at-risk student identification via graph networks, Elo-based adaptive difficulty), cognitive and affective user modeling (EEG emotion recognition, cognitive state detection with foundation models, phishing decision-making cognitive models), embodied/conversational agents and trust, explainable AI and its effect on user decisions, persuasive/behavior-change health tech, and empirical user studies (longitudinal, between-subjects) alongside some Bayesian/robotics-assistive work. One In Memoriam piece (Sandra Carberry) also appeared, evidencing an active, community-embedded editorial voice. Note: a 'Recommender Systems for Health and Wellbeing' special-issue CFP was found but its deadlines (2019-2020) are long expired -- not current, so excluded from active-CFP claims.

**Methods noted as welcome (WO2, qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** recommender systems (graph/hypergraph, sequential, conversational, contrastive/self-supervised learning, fairness-aware/de-biasing), adaptive learning / intelligent tutoring systems and learning analytics, cognitive and affective user modeling (EEG, cognitive-state detection, foundation models), explainable AI / decision-support user studies, embodied conversational agents, trust and likability studies, persuasive technology / digital health behavior-change interventions, empirical longitudinal and between-subjects user studies, formal/theoretical proposals only if empirically substantiated or implementation-validated
